name: Flomic Global Logistics Ltd
title: Flomic Global Logistics Ltd - 504380 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: H1 FY27 revenue up 28% to INR275.65 cr and EBITDA up 80% to INR28.14 cr, but management attributes growth mainly to freight-rate spikes, not volume; no supply-side discipline evidence beyond small warehouse racking adds.

summary.headline: Flomic's Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 37% YoY to INR156 crore and PAT turned to INR4.32 crore profit, driven largely by freight rate spikes.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR156 crore, up about 37% YoY, with EBITDA of INR16.94 crore (margin 10.88%, up roughly 300 bps) and PAT of INR4.32 crore against a loss of about INR1 crore a year earlier. H1 FY27 revenue was INR275.65 crore (up 28.15%), EBITDA INR28.14 crore (up about 80%) and PAT INR6.39 crore versus a loss of INR3.99 crore. Management attributed most of the growth to sharply higher freight rates on India-US and Latin American lanes, with volumes up about 6-7% in Q1. Warehousing expansion at Bhiwandi (vertical multi-tier and pallet racking) was completed in Q2 with customers already occupying the new space.

segments.name: Sea export
segments.commentary: About 38% of Q2 FY27 revenue (33% in H1 FY27).

segments.name: Air and sea import forwarding
segments.commentary: About 30% of Q2 FY27 revenue (31% in H1 FY27). Freight forwarding overall is about 86% of revenue.

segments.name: Air export
segments.commentary: About 14% of Q2 FY27 revenue (16% in H1 FY27).

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: About 13% of Q2 FY27 revenue (14% in H1 FY27). Target is 17-18% over coming quarters and around 20% of turnover over 3-5 years.

segments.commentary: About 5% of Q2 FY27 revenue (6% in H1 FY27).

guidance_outlook: Warehousing share of revenue to rise from about 13-14% to 17-18% over the coming quarters and about 20% within three to five years, driven by customer-backed expansion.

Warehousing expansion expected to add about INR1 crore annual revenue if the two Bhiwandi additions run at 100% capacity; the 15,000 sq ft storage adds about INR50 lakh a year and the 2,000+ pallet positions about INR40-50 lakh once occupied.
H2 FY27 priorities: scale warehousing to customer demand, strengthen project cargo and specialized logistics, deepen integrated services with existing customers, and use technology for efficiency.
Management said freight rate elevation is not uniform across routes and that margin, not rate movement, is the focus; no formal numerical guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Bhiwandi multi-tier storage (ground plus three tiers) commissioned July 2026 and completed September 2026; adds 15,000 sq ft, lifting leasable area of the same footprint from 5,000 to 20,000 sq ft; purchased outright, not leased. Quick commerce customer occupying since September.

Long-span pallet racking (G plus five levels) installed September-October 2026, adding more than 2,000 pallet positions and taking the Bhiwandi warehouse to about 8,000 pallets; FMCG customer occupying since October.
Current overall space utilisation about 97.5%, per management.
Management said racking/shelving investments in existing sites pay back in two to three years; new warehouses are opened only with anchor customers in hand.
Network: 25 branches and more than 30 warehouses across India; new sales offices being considered based on manufacturing and import-export potential.
demand_pricing: Freight rates on India to US 40-foot containers rose from about $2,800 (end February/March) to about $9,600 (August/September), per management; rates doubled to tripled.
Growth in Q2 was described as largely driven by freight rate increases rather than volume; Q1 volume growth was about 6-7%.
Gross margin percentage is roughly constant on freight, so higher turnover lowers GP margin percentage while lifting absolute profit.
Repeat customers were 51% of FY26 business; top 15 customers were more than 20% of turnover. Over 5,000 active customers; more than 42,000 shipments in FY26.
Air freight: contractual space agreements with several carriers; export focus on US, South America and Africa.
Geopolitical disruption (Gulf) has lengthened lead and transit times, but cargo is still moving via alternate routings.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to expand the domestic branch network and location selection criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to opening new sales offices where potential exists; selection is based on manufacturing base and import-export potential of the region.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity and initiatives in air freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Air import and export are both being expanded with carriers on new airport capacity (including Navi Mumbai); export demand is strong, with contractual space agreements and profitability described as good, without figures.

qa_highlights.question: Business mix evolution over 3-5 years, particularly warehousing?
qa_highlights.answer: Warehousing expected to rise from 13-14% to 17-18% and then about 20% of revenue, with investment only where anchor customers exist.

qa_highlights.question: Warehouse strategy: utilisation of existing sites or new leased facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 97.5%; further expansion will be made only if profitable, with racking in existing space paying back in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitical issues and shipping disruptions affecting demand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the situation is unpredictable, but new routings are being found; lead and transit times have risen somewhat, though cargo is moving.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from freight rates versus volumes; what drove EBITDA growth of about 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely freight-rate driven; costs are largely fixed for an asset-light model, so margin gains flow to EBITDA; new software and tight control on employment and other operating costs also helped; interest cost rose with working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Expected annualised revenue and profitability from the Bhiwandi expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR50 lakh a year from the 15,000 sq ft; about INR40-50 lakh from pallet positions once occupied; about INR1 crore total at full utilisation. No profitability figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity in specialised warehousing for e-commerce, quick commerce and FMCG; global partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialised warehousing is seen as a promising growth area; overseas presence is via the WCA network, and future global presence is planned mainly where the company controls cargo flows.

risks_watch: Earnings are heavily tied to freight rate spikes; management acknowledged rate movements are non-uniform and volatile, and gross margin percentage falls as turnover rises.
Interest cost rising with working capital needs as turnover grows.
Geopolitical disruption in the Gulf and other routes is extending transit times.
Bhiwandi occupancy from e-commerce and quick-commerce customers lacks fixed contracts and may fluctuate.
Warehousing share target of 20% depends on continued customer-backed expansion; no capex amount was disclosed for the Bhiwandi works.
Whether margin expansion holds once freight rates normalise, since the H1 PAT base is small (INR6.39 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on results and warehousing growth, but cautious on freight rates, which management repeatedly described as volatile and non-uniform. Answers on geopolitical impacts and air freight were general and lacked figures.
key_quotes: Importantly, this expansion was achieved by optimizing our existing infrastructure without leasing additional space, allowing us to improve capacity utilization.
We just do not build the capacity on the basis of assumptions. If we have anchor tenants in hand, then only we basically tend to expand.
Largely, the growth this year has been driven by the freight rate growth--the growth in terms of the freight rate.

adds.what: Bhiwandi multi-tier storage (ground plus three tiers), adds 15,000 sq ft, lifting leasable area of the footprint from 5,000 to 20,000 sq ft
Bhiwandi long-span pallet racking adding more than 2,000 pallet positions, taking warehouse to about 8,000 pallets

growth.why: No formal numerical guidance; management targets warehousing rising to 17-18% of revenue over coming quarters, backed by two commissioned Bhiwandi additions already occupied by customers (about INR1 crore annual revenue at full utilisation), while Q2 growth was largely freight-rate driven rather than volume.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 10.88% (about +300 bps YoY) with gross margin % roughly constant on freight, but management said margin gains depend on volatile, non-uniform freight rates and no numerical guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bhiwandi multi-tier storage (+15,000 sq ft, footprint 5,000 to 20,000 sq ft) commissioned July-September 2026 and pallet racking (+2,000+ positions, ~8,000 pallets total) installed Sept-Oct 2026, both already part-occupied; these are minor adds, not a large new plant.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 volume grew about 6-7%, but management said Q2 growth was largely freight-rate driven rather than volume; warehousing additions add only about INR1 crore annual revenue at full utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Warehouse utilisation is about 97.5%, so further racking or warehouse space is needed; management said racking in existing sites pays back in 2-3 years and new warehouses open only with anchor customers, and new sales offices are being considered, though no capex amount was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal numerical guidance was given and management described freight rate elevation as non-uniform and volatile, with the focus on margin rather than rate movement, so there is no clear base for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Earnings are heavily tied to freight spikes (India-US 40ft rates rose from about $2,800 to about $9,600), H1 PAT is only INR6.39 crore, interest cost is rising with working capital, and Bhiwandi occupancy lacks fixed contracts.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management listed H2 FY27 priorities of project cargo, specialised logistics and integrated services with existing customers, but no named product launch or date was given.

rows.label: Warehousing share rises to 17-18% of revenue
rows.why: Warehousing is about 13% of Q2 FY27 revenue (14% in H1) and management targets 17-18% over coming quarters, backed by customers already occupying the new Bhiwandi space; the target is conditional on continued customer-backed expansion.

rows.label: Air freight expansion on new airport capacity (Navi Mumbai)
rows.why: Air import and export are being expanded with carriers on new airport capacity and contractual space agreements, with export demand described as strong, but no figures were given.

rows.label: Freight rate normalisation risk
rows.why: Freight rates on India-US 40ft lanes rose about 3x (from $2,800 to $9,600), so a normalisation would reverse much of the margin and EBITDA gain that drove H1 PAT of INR6.39 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on warehousing growth and the Bhiwandi occupancy, but cautious and general on freight rate volatility, geopolitical disruption and air freight, giving no figures; analysts pushed on how much growth came from freight rates versus volume and on the Bhiwandi economics.
